# Quirks and Features of Quarto

## R Code Options

In Quarto, we have many options to decide whether the code chunks will run, show results, or anything in between. This is very useful, because we often want to customize exactly what we see, rather than having everything run all at once. So, for this exercise, we will customize these options.

## Figure Customization in R

Sometimes, we may want to customize our figures. Here are some options:

- `fig-cap`: Captions

- `fig-alt`: Alt text

- `fig-width`: Width of the figure

- `fig-height`: Height of the figure

- `label`: This allows you to relabel the figure which must start with \`\@fig-\`

## Callout Blocks

There are five types of callout blocks:

- note

- Warning

- important

- tip

- caution

They each will add a box highlighting the contents needed. We will try each of them as see how they look.

## Citations

In your project, you will likely be citing sources for your dataset, some background research, and other results you may find useful. In your other classes, you may have used one of the following methods:

- Manual citation
- Zotero
- Google Doc plug-ins
- Online citation generators

For Quarto, none of these are very useful or efficient. You can theoretically do everything by hand by typing out the citations, but this is tedious and hard to format in R. So, we will introduce a citation system with `bibTeX` files. The citations will be placed at the end of the document.
